Celebrity Crypto Conman

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Bitcoin investors have lost hundreds of thousands of rands after depositing their money into a digital vault

Unique Selling Point:
Hundreds of thousands of rands invested into a bitcoin scheme are missing, the money has vanished and so has the guy who promised to triple these investments. Loyal listeners of Thobela FM responded to an advert about a chance to make money via a crypto currency scheme, at the forefront was Sebasa Mogale a drive time radio dj at the station and actor on popular SABC hit series Skeem Saam.

The untrained investors who bought into this, left their jobs, cashed out their pension and savings and took up bank loans to invest into Sebasa's bitcoin scheme. They had dreams to build homes, create wealth, send their kids to better schools but they are left broke, depressed and desperate.


Summary:
The advent of crypto currency has opened up investment opportunities for the ordinary and wealth creation is no longer in the hands of finance experts. What used be exclusive knowledge can now be accessed via digital means with countless tutorials on Youtube and success stories on the internet, making money via crypto seems easy and no one wants to be left behind. Bitcoin became a buzzword and the crypto curious did not want miss the gravy train.

Many of the people who signed up to join Sebasa Mogase's bitcoin investment scheme will tell that whilst they were not entirely sure on the technical detail and didn't fully understand the jargon, they were sold on it. Sebasa was a voice they'd heard almost daily on the radio, on a station they'd trusted as a legitimate source of information. This radio man did not move alone, he was always in the company of Mpho Dagada who'd become a millionaire at 21 through bitcoin business and was one of the president's advisor's on advancing 4IR. There was nothing to question, the evidence of his wealth was there and his proximity to power sold him as the guy that can make your dreams come true.

People signed and no sign of the moolah, were these naive investors sold a pipe dream or were they victims of a market downtown.
This and many questions remain unanswered, Sebasa has continued to ignore this cohort of people who poured money into his scheme. Yet he and his millionaire friend roll-out new bitcoin investment schemes and sign up eager recruits who don't want to miss the gravy train.

Script:


William Makhura was a traffic officer for over two decades in Polokwane, Limpopo. Now a pensioner, the soft spoken lone figure, enjoys life at a slower pace, tending his garden.
But something he heard on his favourite radio station would shatter this peaceful existence.




Three years ago, William was looking for ways to stretch his pension when a scheme advertised on Thobela FM caught his attention.

It promised that with a small investment through bitcoin, he could make guaranteed returns.




WILL: when you invest daai deng 12 thousand eh month end you will earn 2 thousand. So I said oh ja no this is a good thing.
So in went his first investment of R24 000 and days later, he added more…

William:
On the 20th august 2020 I deposited 82 thousand
03;42 Mac – 82 thousand, where was this money coming from Ntate William
3;47 Will – I was a pensioner.
3;50 Mac – so you used your pension –Will yes
Presented by popular SABC radio host Sebasa Mogale and self-made millionaire and author Mpho Dagada… it was this highly persuasive seminar that sealed the deal…

And he wasn’t alone…
In Johannesburg, electrical engineer Alpheus Makolane was in the middle of building a dream home for his family back in Limpopo. The father of three and his wife had saved up over R 200 000 to complete the construction.

He too attended a seminar and the sales-pitch was convincing…
Alpheus; 3;32 – The joining fee was R235 000, I was going to get it back after 3 years, after the contract expires. I’d get my 235 thousand back and every month, my returns would not be less than 30 thousand for a period of 3 years.

The earnings sounded great and few risks were spelled out.. so 34-year-old Sello Bonoko also signed up for an investment that would help him start a business and acquire a home for his growing family.
Sello: no one could resist it, the amount that they were promising. …if eh you invest 235 you will be getting eeh 50 thousand monthly for the coming 3 years
4;48 Mac – you saw yourself hitting the big time – uno bona upopile
4;49 - 5;03 Sello – Yes to an extent that I had to ask a question that, what you’re saying there are you talking about guaranteed amounts and then him, Sebasa Mogale himself said yes its guaranteed amounts.
Mac 6;20 When you went into that seminar, did you know anything about bitcoin or cryptocurrency
6;24 Sello – hm no I was a bit clueless, I’d just heard bitcoin bitcoin, it’s making people wealthy.
Mac Link – With crypto currency the road to riches is paved in gold. Your wealth is at your fingertips and with so many self-made millionaires already, no one wants to miss the gravy train.
But while cryptocurrency has made many people lots of money, and disrupted the financial world in the last decade…it is unregulated there are no accounting standards.

On top of that the crypto market is highly volatile – even the most experienced investor can be undone overnight.
In this market, Mogale and Dagada fashioned themselves as crypto currency hotshots and set about recruiting investors….

Flyers were splashed on their social media pages, and adverts were on regular rotation on Thobela FM.


CAR LINK; On air each afternoon, for many listeners he’s become a familiar and trusted voice. No doubt then, that his investors thought the different bitcoin and crypto schemes were credible and indeed lucrative.
Mogale and Dagada were intermediaries…marketing the investment products and services of Mining City - a global bitcoin mining platform founded in 2019, that claimed to be the world’s most successful mining community.

Bitcoin mining, the process of finding and creating new bitcoin using a series of computers and software, is extremely pricey and energy intensive.

Bitcoin Vault was just one of the investment projects that Mogale and Dagada championed - where investors were sold different packages - the most lucrative being the platinum package where a R200,000 deposit would yield high returns for a period of three years.

In late 2020, Sello invested R235 000.




Sello: I got the money from my savings and then eh the child savings as well, I took everything I was saving for the children..

Keep Mac’s reaction here..

Once the lump sum was transferred, Sello expected his first payout.
7;38 Mac – how much did you get in the first month
7;40 Sello – the first month, absolutely nothing
7;41 Mac – second month
7;42 Sello – Nothing
08;12 Mac – are you panicking at this time.
08;18 Sello – ah not really I wasn’t panicking, I was still confident ehm because ehm, they have a group chat.

the things they used to say, you’d think ah no, I’m still on the right track.
The road to riches was starting to show cracks but Sello and many others were still trusting the promises.

Internationally though, financial markets were raising alarm and governments were banning crypto mining platforms like Mining City, due to its high electricity use.
5;05 I put in trusted reviews mining city and immediately the reviews came back saying this is a ponzi scheme
Attorney Maurice Crespi specialises in crypto currency and digital technologies.

He looked into the schemes marketed by Mogale and Dagada.
05;32 Maurice – well firstly, they do not appear to be crypto experts in the mining field, mining is very very different. You’re not buying crypto. You’re actually paying a company to mine crypto on your behalf. …eh further red flags would be the mere fact that they promised these returns,Now if you promise these returns you gotta ask yourself why is the company itself not actually investing in these returns why is it that the company actually requires clients to actually invest. 6;12 to make these returns as opposed to them making them themselves.
We sent a list of questions to Mining City, but there has been no response.

Sello’s dream was crumbling.

Unemployed and now in serious debt, he was forced to move back home. He couldn’t even afford to buy clothes for his 11month old son.
13;29 Sello: I’m using the sister’s clothes because I still had them.
Alpheus: 13;12 eish, it was a serious problem with my wife, she even left me and went back home.
We set off to Limpopo for answers, but Sebasa Mogale wasn’t broadcasting as he usually does from the Polokwane studios. We pressed him for an interview.




Our search continued in another part of town. Mac Reading email: We just got an email from Sebasa whilst shooting, he insists he doesn’t see the necessity of an interview. Saying investors were given a clear presentation on how the investments worked…




At the office, I ran into the landlord who said Sebasa has been struggling to pay rent. Office Link: This was Sebasa’s business headquarters. In here was I.T support and admin staff. There was an open door policy.
But with no warning, it closed down and the furniture was moved.
Mpho Dagada equally didn’t respond to our emails, so we called his office - we were iced out by one of the secretaries.




So we called again, but it was clear that Dagada would not speak to us.
Phonecall: 5;40 Okay cause I just I spoke to him and he said he told the previous assistant, to say no comment. He can’t speak on behalf of (Mining city), I’m not sure if they did it then, I’m not sure.

6;34 ooh heke it’s a tricky one yazi,me I’m just an employee.

08;28 Mac – what steps can aggrieved investors take to try and recoup their money, 08;34 Brandon in my experience an aggrieved investor will hardly every get their money back. And that is why we say to people stay away from unregistered financial products.

Brandon Topham heads Investigations and Enforcement at the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.
07;44 Brandon – the problem with crypto assets, worldwide, is that it’s a new technology and regulation can’t just run into something blindly. we are working hard at it for the last 2 years. I believe the first set of legislation in this regard should be coming out eminently
After a year of trying to reach him, Sebasa blocked his investors on WhatsApp and they say he ignores their calls.
11; 13 Mac – And here what’s this
11; 15 Sello – this was the conversation I had with him, showing him all these things that they are dealing with are scams. I did my research,
12;44 Mac – Sello but this is research you should have done before you took out your money
12;50 Sello: it’s very much difficult when its someone you know and trust,
Disenfranchised, the investors have had no choice but to pick up the pieces of their lives after the catastrophic losses. At least 140 investors hold out hope that they might be compensated, as they continue to wait for answers.
